**4th AF transmittal of ATC Weekly Intelligence Summary extract** to FBI San Francisco. Letter from HQ Fourth Air Force, A-2 Intelligence, Hamilton Field, California, file 4AFDA 333.5/1208-I, dated **27 August 1947**. Signed Donald L. Springer, Lt. Colonel, GSC, AC of S, A-2. (FBI ref 62-29387.)

**Extracted from:** Weekly Intelligence Summary, Air Transport Command, Washington 25, D.C., dated 20 August 1947, Copy No. 120, Article I, p. 1.

**Verbatim extract — 'FLYING OBJECTS IN GUAM':**
'Unidentified flying objects have been observed by **three American enlisted men of the 147th Airways and Air Communications Service Squadron at Harmon Field, Guam.** The men report that at **1040 hours on 14 August 1947** the **two objects, which they describe as small, crescent-shaped** and traveling at a **speed twice that of a fighter plane,** passed over them on a **zig-zag course in a westerly direction** at an approximate altitude of **1,200 feet.** The objects disappeared into clouds and a few seconds later a similar object possibly one of those previously observed, emerged from the clouds and proceeded west. No further details have been reported.'

**Note:** One of the earliest documented UAP sightings from the Western Pacific by U.S. military personnel during the 1947 flying-disc wave. The crescent-shape description is striking and predates many later 'flying wing' classifications.

**原文摘录——"关岛的飞行物体"：**
"不明飞行物体被**第147航路与航空通信勤务中队驻关岛哈蒙机场的三名美国士兵**观察到。这些士兵报告称，在**1947年8月14日1040时**，**两个物体，他们描述为小型、新月形状**，以**战斗机两倍的速度**飞行，以**之字形航线向西方向**在大约**1,200英尺**的高度从他们上方经过。这些物体消失在云层中，几秒钟后一个类似的物体——可能是之前观察到的其中一个——从云层中出现并继续向西飞行。未报告更多细节。"

**COPY — Air Rescue Service, Detachment 8 (62d AAF BU), McChord Field, Tacoma, Washington.** Subject: Final Mission Report. To: Commanding Officer, Air Rescue Service, MacDill Field, Florida. Dated **4 August 1947**.

**Mission Number 39.**

**Nature:** At 04:00 PST on 1 August 1947, Army Flight Service notified this detachment that a plane had been seen to crash and burn **thirteen (13) miles south of Kelso, Washington (46°N 122°48'W).**

**Action taken:** At 04:30 PST, ARS received information from Mr. C. C. Clark, local sheriff of Kelso, Wash., that the scene of the crash was 15 to 20 miles south of the town and was difficult to reach in the vicinity of Castle Creek. The Kelso Chief of Police saw an aircraft fly low over the town, then crash and burn to the west. The time was about 0235 PST. A check of aircraft known to be in the vicinity revealed that **B-25 #115 had departed McChord Field at 0212 PST for Hamilton Field, California.** Weather was reported CFR. A call soon made visibility exceptionally good. The pilot's name was **Capt. W. L. Davidson**; the aircrew were three (3) additional persons.

**Investigation:** Base Operations Officer and Base PIO were notified. This detachment began organizing a ground party of base personnel to supplement that being formed by the Kelso Chief of Police. At 05:00 PST information was received from Kelso by ABS that ground fog in the valleys at the scene of the crash was preventing the ground party from leaving the planes. Since no communication had been received from B-25 #115, it was assumed that it was the plane reported as crashed. ARS C-47 was pre-flighted to transport the Army ground party to Kelso, but a check of the field conditions there deemed it advisable to use a smaller aircraft. Of the two C-45s available, one belonging to ARS was unserviced after a night flight; the other, belonging to AACS, was readied even though a responsible officer of that organization was not present to authorize the flight. Fog at Kelso prevented take-off until 07:00 PST. The ground party, led by Capt. W. L. Littrell and Capt. T. M. Forberg, consisted of six men including a medical technician and a photographer. At 00:00 PST, the Kelso Chief of Police notified ARS that a passenger of the crashed airplane was in his office and had confirmed.

**Note:** This is the **famous B-25 crash that killed Capt Davidson and Lt Brown**, the two 4th AF CIC officers who had interviewed Fred Crisman and Harold Dahl about the Maury Island incident two days earlier in Tacoma. Their deaths fueled decades of UFO conspiracy speculation about the Maury Island case.

**副本 — 空中救援服务部队，第8分遣队（第62 AAF BU），麦科德机场，华盛顿州塔科马。** 主题：最终任务报告。致：空中救援服务部队指挥官，麦克迪尔机场，佛罗里达州。日期 **1947年8月4日**。

**任务编号39。**

**性质：** 1947年8月1日太平洋标准时间04:00，陆军飞行服务部门通知本分遣队，有一架飞机被目击坠毁并起火，**位于华盛顿州凯尔索以南十三(13)英里处（北纬46°西经122°48'）。**

**采取的行动：** 太平洋标准时间04:30，空中救援服务部队从凯尔索当地警长C. C. 克拉克先生处获悉，坠机现场位于该镇以南15至20英里处，在城堡溪附近难以到达。凯尔索警察局长看到一架飞机低空飞过该镇，然后在西面坠毁并起火。时间约为太平洋标准时间02:35。对已知在该区域的飞机进行检查后发现，**B-25 #115号机已于太平洋标准时间02:12从麦科德机场起飞前往加利福尼亚州汉密尔顿机场。** 天气报告为CFR。呼叫很快使能见度变得极好。飞行员姓名为**W. L. 戴维森上尉**；机组人员另有三(3)人。

**调查：** 基地作战军官和基地公共信息官已获通知。本分遣队开始组织一支由基地人员组成的地面小组，以补充凯尔索警察局长正在组建的队伍。太平洋标准时间05:00，空中救援服务部队从凯尔索收到信息，坠机现场山谷中的地面雾正在阻止地面小组离开平地。由于未收到B-25 #115号机的任何通讯，因此推定它就是报告坠毁的飞机。空中救援服务部队的C-47运输机已完成飞行前检查，准备将陆军地面小组运送至凯尔索，但对当地机场条件的检查认为使用较小型飞机更为可取。在两架可用的C-45中，一架属于空中救援服务部队的飞机在夜间飞行后未完成维护；另一架属于AACS的飞机已准备就绪，尽管该组织的负责军官不在场授权此次飞行。凯尔索的雾直到太平洋标准时间07:00才允许起飞。由W. L. 利特雷尔上尉和T. M. 福伯格上尉率领的地面小组由六人组成，包括一名医疗技术员和一名摄影师。太平洋标准时间00:00，凯尔索警察局长通知空中救援服务部队，坠毁飞机的一名乘客在他办公室，并已确认。

**注：** 这就是**导致戴维森上尉和布朗中尉丧生的著名B-25坠机事件**，这两名第4航空队CIC（反情报队）军官曾在两天前于塔科马就莫里岛(Maury Island)事件询问过弗雷德·克里斯曼(Fred Crisman)和哈罗德·达尔(Harold Dahl)。他们的死亡在此后数十年间引发了关于莫里岛案件的UFO阴谋论猜测。

events.report_summary:
Sworn AFFIDAVIT given on 14 July 1947 in the State of California, County of Kern, by Jeannette Marie Scott — Secretary to 1st Lt J. C. McHenry, Billeting Officer at Muroc Army Air Field (now Edwards AFB), Muroc, California. Stationed on base for approximately eighteen months and familiar with all types of aircraft.

On Tuesday morning, 8 July 1947, at approximately 10:20 AM, while typing some cards, Lt McHenry called Scott (along with T/Sgt Joseph Ruvolo and S/Sgt Gerald E. Naumann) to the front of B.O.Q. 'B' Building. Pointing directly above them, he asked them to explain what they saw. Scott observed two silver-colored, disc-like objects flying toward Mojave, California, one directly behind the other, at approximately 300 to 400 miles per hour at an altitude of approximately 8,000 feet. She listened carefully for several minutes and heard no engine drone such as would be expected from any aircraft. She ruled out weather balloons (due to the horizontal flight attitude) and birds (due to the definite metallic reflection from the sun's rays).

About three or four minutes after the two objects had nearly disappeared, Scott sighted a third object — similar in appearance, silver-colored, disc-shaped — flying in a tight circle at approximately 8,000 feet, neither gaining nor losing altitude. She concluded this third object could not be a weather balloon (horizontal flight) nor any conventional aircraft (tight circle).

Witnessed by Thomas A. McMillan. The statement was given freely and voluntarily without threats or promises under duress; Scott swore she was of sound mind and body and that the statement was true to the best of her knowledge and belief.

**Note:** this 8 July 1947 Muroc sighting is one of the documented early-era reports from Edwards/Muroc AFB during the original 'flying disc' wave.

events.report_summary_zh:
1947年7月14日在加利福尼亚州克恩县(State of California, County of Kern)宣誓的书面证词，由珍妮特·玛丽·斯科特(Jeannette Marie Scott)提供——她是穆罗克陆军航空基地(Muroc Army Air Field,现爱德华兹空军基地Edwards AFB)驻地军官J.C.麦克亨利(J. C. McHenry)一级中尉的秘书，基地位于加利福尼亚州穆罗克(Muroc, California)。她在基地驻扎约十八个月，熟悉各类型飞行器。

1947年7月8日星期二上午约10点20分，斯科特在打字录入卡片时，麦克亨利中尉召唤她(连同技术军士约瑟夫·鲁沃洛Joseph Ruvolo和参谋军士杰拉尔德·E·诺曼Gerald E. Naumann)来到军官宿舍'B'楼(B.O.Q. 'B' Building)前方。他指向正上方，询问他们看到了什么。斯科特观察到两个银色的、碟状物体正朝加利福尼亚州莫哈韦(Mojave, California)方向飞行,一个紧跟在另一个后面，速度约每小时300至400英里，高度约8,000英尺。她仔细聆听了数分钟，没有听到任何飞行器应有的引擎轰鸣声。她排除了气象气球的可能性(因为是水平飞行姿态)和鸟类的可能性(因为有明确的太阳光线金属反射)。

在这两个物体几乎消失约三到四分钟后，斯科特目击到第三个物体——外观相似，银色、碟形——在约8,000英尺高度做紧密圆周飞行，既不爬升也不下降。她断定这第三个物体不可能是气象气球(水平飞行)，也不可能是任何常规飞行器(紧密盘旋)。

由托马斯·A·麦克米伦(Thomas A. McMillan)见证。该陈述系自由、自愿提供，没有任何威胁、承诺或胁迫；斯科特宣誓她神志清醒、身体健康，且该陈述在她所知所信范围内完全真实。

**Note:** 这起1947年7月8日穆罗克目击事件是爱德华兹/穆罗克空军基地(Edwards/Muroc AFB)在最初"飞碟"浪潮期间有记录的早期报告之一。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Confidential report 4AF-1208-I concerning unidentified object sighting near Placerville, California.

**Witnesses:** On 26 August 1947, S/A Hubbard and the agent contacted Ray Switzer, Insurance Adjustor at the Raffels Hotel, Placerville. After traveling Cedar Ravine Road to a point nine miles southeast of Placerville (known as Buck's Bar), Switzer decided the observation location from 14 August 1947 was nearer to Placerville. After a thorough check of the road, Switzer believed he observed the object on the ridge just north of Webber Creek where the road breaks over the summit.

**Location Details:** Observation point located two miles from Raffels Hotel, Placerville, California, on the Cedar Ravine Road. Precise coordinates: 38° 42' 45" North Latitude and 120° 47' 16" West Longitude. Elevation: 2,000 feet above sea level. The horizon from this point in the south is formed by a series of mountain peaks lying generally through 389° 39' 45" and on the south side of Squaw Hollow Creek, four miles distant, ranging in elevation from 3,300 feet to 4,500 feet above sea level.

**Observation:** Switzer was not definite about what part of his field of view he had seen the object and indicated it could have been as far as the horizon. Any object or particles of an object, Switzer stated, would be in a six square mile area of wooded, mountainous terrain full of canyons and ravines.

**Agent's Notes:** The agent believes Switzer could have seen an aluminum surfaced conventional type aircraft which, due to the distance at which he observed it, had distinguishing features not seen because of the bright reflection and the very short period of observation. The aircraft would have been coming from the left as Switzer turned to the left, thereby giving the effect of much greater speed than the object was really traveling. This agent has no explanation as to the smoke trail observed by Switzer. If reconnaissance is desired to see if anything can be located on the ground, agent suggests a small type aircraft similar to an L-5 be used at low level flight between the hours of 1100 to 1300. Switzer was very cooperative and expended much time in an effort to be of as much service as possible. Switzer will communicate with the AC of S, HQ, Fourth Air Force, Hamilton Field, California, in the event of any reports of aircraft wreckage in the area.

**Additional Information:** On 26 August 1947, a check with Ranger Dixon, State Forest Service, Camino, California, and George S. Young, Forester, Federal Forest Service, Placerville, California, revealed there had been no forest fires or reported aircraft crashes in the area in question within the last month.

**Report by:** Bryden E. Moon, Special Agent, 4AF CIO

**Witnesses:** 1947年8月26日，特别探员Hubbard与另一名探员在普莱瑟维尔的Raffels酒店联系了保险理算员Ray Switzer。沿Cedar Ravine Road行驶至普莱瑟维尔东南9英里处(称为Buck's Bar)后，Switzer认定1947年8月14日的观测地点更靠近普莱瑟维尔。经过对道路的彻底检查，Switzer相信他是在Webber Creek以北、道路翻越山顶处的山脊上观察到该物体的。

**Location Details:** 观测点位于加利福尼亚州普莱瑟维尔Raffels酒店沿Cedar Ravine Road方向2英里处。精确坐标:北纬38° 42' 45"，西经120° 47' 16"。海拔:海拔2,000英尺。从该点向南的地平线由一系列山峰构成，大致位于389° 39' 45"方向，在Squaw Hollow Creek南侧，距离4英里，海拔高度从3,300英尺到4,500英尺不等。

**Observation:** Switzer对于在其视野中哪个部位看到该物体并不确定，表示该物体可能远至地平线处。Switzer称，任何物体或物体碎片都可能位于6平方英里范围内，该区域为布满峡谷和沟壑的树木繁茂的山地地形。

**Agent's Notes:** 该探员认为Switzer可能看到的是一架铝制表面的常规型飞机，由于观察距离较远，加之强烈的反光和极短的观察时间，未能看清其显著特征。该飞机可能是从左侧飞来，正好Switzer向左转身，从而产生了比物体实际速度快得多的效果。本探员无法解释Switzer观察到的烟迹。如需进行侦察以查看地面是否有任何可定位物，探员建议使用类似L-5的小型飞机在1100至1300时之间进行低空飞行。Switzer非常配合，花费了大量时间努力提供尽可能多的帮助。如该地区有任何飞机残骸报告，Switzer将与位于加利福尼亚州Hamilton Field的第四航空队总部参谋长助理(AC of S, HQ, Fourth Air Force)联系。

**Additional Information:** 1947年8月26日，与加利福尼亚州卡米诺(Camino, California)州森林服务局护林员Dixon以及加利福尼亚州普莱瑟维尔联邦森林服务局林务员George S. Young核实，过去一个月内该问题区域未发生森林火灾或飞机坠毁报告。

**Report by:** Bryden E. Moon，特别探员，4AF CIO

events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** Administrative directive D 333.5 (CIB) from Headquarters Air Defense Command at Mitchel Air Force Base, New York, establishing formal procedures for investigating and reporting "Flying Disc" incidents.

**Recipients:** Commanding Generals of First, Second, Fourth, Tenth, Eleventh, and Fourteenth Air Forces, Air Defense Command.

**Purpose:** This confidential memorandum establishes command-wide protocols for handling flying disc reports. Numbered air forces under Air Defense Command are made responsible for prompt investigation and reporting of flying disc incidents occurring within their respective areas.

**Investigation Guidelines:** After evaluating incidents, A-2s (intelligence officers) will determine investigation extent. The directive emphasizes that "futile expenditure of military funds and manpower must be avoided." Flying discs are to be investigated per Counter Intelligence Incident Cases procedures, following USAF Operating Intelligence Echelon structure.

**Witness Corroboration Requirements:** When witnesses who were together at time of incident are widely separated at time of investigation, only one witness need be interrogated to corroborate each other's story.

**Hoax/Publicity Protocol:** If reasonable indication exists that a reported incident is a hoax or fabrication by publicity seekers, no further investigative effort will be expended. Reports of such circumstances will be submitted to the FBI office concerned.

**Reporting Structure:** Two report types mandated: (a) Spot Reports (fragmentary) submitted on all incidents, followed by Letter Reports; (b) Letter Reports submitted upon completed investigation. Reports to be narrative style, covering only pertinent facts. Duplicate copies usually sent by regular mail, though substantial incidents may warrant expedited transmission.

**FBI Coordination:** Investigations coordinated with FBI Office per instructions in letter D 333.3 EX dated 3 September 1947, subject "Cooperation of FBI with AAF on Investigation of 'Flying Disc' Incidents."

**CIC Personnel:** Counter Intelligence Corps personnel attached to numbered air forces may be utilized to prosecute investigations.

**Document Reference:** ENCLOSURE (2-4-9334-140)

events.report_summary_zh:
**Document Type:** 来自纽约米切尔空军基地(Mitchel Air Force Base)总部防空司令部的行政指令D 333.5 (CIB),建立了调查和报告"飞碟"事件的正式程序。

**Recipients:** 第一、第二、第四、第十、第十一和第十四空军司令部将军,防空司令部。

**Purpose:** 这份机密备忘录建立了处理飞碟报告的全司令部协议。防空司令部下属的各编号空军负责对各自辖区内发生的飞碟事件进行及时调查和报告。

**Investigation Guidelines:** 在评估事件后,A-2(情报官员)将决定调查范围。该指令强调"必须避免军事资金和人力的无谓消耗"。飞碟调查应按照反情报事件案件程序进行,遵循USAF作战情报梯队结构。

**Witness Corroboration Requirements:** 当事件发生时在一起的目击者在调查时相距甚远时,只需询问其中一名目击者即可相互印证彼此的陈述。

**Hoax/Publicity Protocol:** 如果有合理迹象表明所报告的事件是寻求宣传者的恶作剧或捏造,将不再投入进一步的调查工作。此类情况的报告将提交给相关的FBI办公室。

**Reporting Structure:** 要求提交两种类型的报告:(a) 现场报告(片段性),针对所有事件提交,随后提交信函报告;(b) 信函报告,在完成调查后提交。报告应采用叙述性风格,仅涵盖相关事实。副本通常通过普通邮件发送,但重大事件可采用加急传输方式。

**FBI Coordination:** 调查工作需与FBI办公室协调配合,依据1947年9月3日D 333.3 EX号信函中的指示进行,主题为"FBI与AAF就'飞碟'事件调查的合作"。

**CIC Personnel:** 可利用派驻编号空军的反情报部队(Counter Intelligence Corps)人员执行调查。

events.report_summary:
**Letter** from Headquarters Air Materiel Command (MCIAXO-3/JWA/saw), Wright-Patterson AF Base, dated **9 September 1948**. Routed to: Director, Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Department of Justice, Washington D.C. — **ATTN: FBI Laboratory.** Subject: **Project 'SIGN'** (the original USAF UAP investigation program, predecessor to Project Grudge and Project Blue Book).

**Enclosure:** A small sample of soil, taken from a depression reputedly caused by a **'flying saucer'** — described as being approximately **10 feet in diameter and 1 foot thick**, which supposedly settled gently to the ground, **rebounded to a height of about 20 feet, and then continued on its journey.** Although the depression was immediately covered by a large washtub, a heavy rain subsequently filled it about one-third full of water before any sample of dirt could be taken.

**Request to FBI Laboratory:** Analyze and test the soil sample. AMC wants to ascertain in particular: (1) if there are traces of unusual elements or alloys adhering to the surface of the particles, or (2) if any abnormality in structure exists showing that the soil was subjected to intense heat, gases, or radioactive substances. AMC notes that no comparative 'surrounding soil' sample was collected (an oversight), so a comparison cannot be made at this time. If results are anomalous, AMC could arrange to procure surrounding soil for comparative analysis.

**Status:** The accompanying sample has not been tested by any other agency, nor will it be — making this analysis an exclusive AMC-FBI cooperation.

**Note:** A landmark Project SIGN document — the first known instance of physical trace evidence (soil from a UAP landing site) being submitted by AMC to the FBI Laboratory for elemental and structural analysis.

**Letter**，发自空军装备司令部总部（MCIAXO-3/JWA/saw），莱特-帕特森空军基地(Wright-Patterson AF Base)，日期为**1948年9月9日**。收件人：联邦调查局局长，美国司法部，华盛顿特区——**收件部门：FBI实验室。** 主题：**"符号"项目**（即Project 'SIGN'，USAF最初的UAP调查计划，后被"怨恨"项目和"蓝皮书"项目取代）。

**附件：** 一小份土壤样本，取自据称由一个**"飞碟"**造成的凹陷处——该物体被描述为**直径约10英尺、厚度约1英尺**，据称它轻轻降落到地面，**反弹至约20英尺高，然后继续飞行。** 尽管该凹陷处立即被一个大洗衣盆盖住，但在采集任何土壤样本之前，一场暴雨已将其填满了约三分之一的水。

**对FBI实验室的请求：** 分析和检测该土壤样本。AMC特别希望确定：（1）颗粒表面是否有不寻常元素或合金的痕迹附着，或（2）是否存在任何结构异常，表明土壤曾受到强热、气体或放射性物质的影响。AMC指出，没有采集对比用的"周围土壤"样本（这是一个疏忽），因此目前无法进行比较。如果结果异常，AMC可以安排获取周围土壤进行对比分析。

**状态：** 所附样本尚未经任何其他机构检测，也不会送往其他机构——这使得本次分析成为AMC与FBI的独家合作。

The records include high-profile incident accounts, photographic evidence from sites like Oak Ridge, TN, and technical proposals regarding potential propulsion systems. events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** Official response letter from NEPA Project (Nuclear Energy for the Propulsion of Aircraft) to U.S. Atomic Energy Commission Security Division regarding photographic analysis.

**Background:** This letter dated 10 February 1949 responds to a 16 December 1948 inquiry about photographs taken during July 1947 by Mr. William Presley of 218 Illinois Avenue, Oak Ridge, Tennessee, showing an unidentified object flying over Oak Ridge.

**Analysis Process:** The NEPA Project office forwarded the material to the Air Force office of the Chief, Technical Intelligence Division, Intelligence Department, Air Materiel Command, at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Dayton, Ohio for professional evaluation.

**Findings:** The Air Force analysis revealed technical defects in the photographic negatives. When examined under strong incident light, the emulsion was "raised at that point above the normal level of the remaining emulsion," indicating that either a drop of warm water or developer struck the film at that location and rolled down, affecting both the negative containing the sphere and the succeeding negative. When two negatives were placed side by side with film edges aligned, the "trail" was continuous and matched between sections, confirming the drop rolled from one negative to the next. The fogged edge of the negative containing only the trail provided additional proof, as the trail extended beyond the normal film format.

**Conclusion:** The photographs were determined to be artifacts caused by photographic processing errors, not genuine images of an aerial object.

**Document Type:** 来自NEPA项目（飞机核能推进项目）致美国原子能委员会安全部门关于照片分析的官方回复函。

**Background:** 这封日期为1949年2月10日的信函，回复了1948年12月16日关于照片的询问，这些照片由田纳西州橡树岭(Oak Ridge, Tennessee)伊利诺伊大道218号的威廉·普雷斯利先生(William Presley)于1947年7月拍摄，显示一个不明物体飞越橡树岭上空。

**Analysis Process:** NEPA项目办公室将该材料转交给位于俄亥俄州代顿市赖特-帕特森空军基地(Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Dayton, Ohio)的空军航空器材司令部情报部技术情报处处长办公室进行专业评估。

**Findings:** 空军分析显示照片底片存在技术缺陷。在强入射光下检查时，乳剂在该点"高于其余乳剂的正常水平"，表明一滴温水或显影液落在胶片该位置并向下滚动，同时影响了包含球体的底片和后续底片。当将两张底片边缘对齐并排放置时，"痕迹"是连续的，并且在各部分之间相匹配，证实了液滴从一张底片滚动到下一张底片。仅包含痕迹的底片边缘雾化提供了额外证据，因为痕迹延伸超出了正常胶片格式范围。

**Conclusion:** 这些照片被确定为由照片冲洗错误造成的伪影，而非真实的空中物体图像。

events.record_description: The FBI's 62-HQ-83894 case file includes investigative records, eyewitness testimonies, and public reports concerning Unidentified Flying Objects and flying discs documented between June 1947 and July 1968. The records include high-profile incident accounts, photographic evidence from sites like Oak Ridge, TN, and technical proposals regarding potential propulsion systems. events.report_summary:
**Source:** Draft message from HQ 18th OSI Dist Office at Offutt AFB, Omaha, Nebraska to Dir of Special Investigations HQ USAF, Washington D.C., dated 16 January 1950. References information from Wyandotte Echo newspaper, Kansas City, Kansas, 6 January 1950.

**Witness:** Rudy Fick, a well-known Kansas City auto dealer, stopped in Denver approximately 2 weeks prior (early January 1950) while returning from Ogden, Utah. At that time he called on the manager of Ford Agency.

**Sighting:** Fick stated flying saucers from Venus came to earth by accident. During conversation, Fick was meeting with a man named Coulter who had arrived seeking a meeting. Coulter revealed startling information about crashing "the Gate" at a radar station near New Mexico and driving hostages. While there he saw 2 of the highly secret "Flying Saucers."

**Object:** Spot report details the Flying Saucers: one was damaged and the other almost perfectly intact. They consisted of 2 parts, a cockpit or cabin about 6 feet in diameter. A ring 18 feet across and 2 feet thick surrounded the cabin. The cabin was constructed of metal resembling aluminum, but actual analysis of the metal has defied analysis. Coulter possessed a piece of metal and gave it to the Ford man to send to Dearborn plant for analysis. This man (Coulter) showed the group, including Fick, a clock or automatic calendar which was taken from one of the Flying Saucers. This clock or automatic calendar consisted of 3 pieces of metal together with some unusual type of metal. On the face of 1 or 2 pieces of the metal there appeared an indentation which rotated around the disk completing a cycle each 24 days.

**Context:** According to information given, around 50 of these Flying saucers have been found in the United States in a period of 2 years. Of these, 40 are in the 7 US Research Channels in Los Angeles. Each craft had a crew of 2. The bodies in the damaged ship were charred, but the other ship's occupants were in a perfect state of preservation, although dead.

**Note:** Document is a relay of a Category Baker (intelligence) message originally sent 14 January 1950.

**Source:** 1950年1月16日,位于内布拉斯加州奥马哈市奥富特空军基地(Offutt AFB)的第18特别调查处总部发给华盛顿特区美国空军总部特别调查处主任的电报草稿。引用了1950年1月6日堪萨斯州堪萨斯城《怀恩多特回声报》(Wyandotte Echo)的信息。

**Witness:** Rudy Fick,堪萨斯城一位知名汽车经销商,在从犹他州奥格登(Ogden, Utah)返回途中于大约两周前(1950年1月初)在丹佛(Denver)停留。当时他拜访了福特代理公司的经理。

**Sighting:** Fick称来自金星的飞碟意外来到地球。在交谈过程中,Fick正在会见一位名叫Coulter的男子,此人特地前来寻求会面。Coulter透露了关于在新墨西哥州附近一个雷达站"强闯大门"并劫持人质的惊人信息。他在那里看到了2个高度机密的"飞碟"。

**Object:** 现场报告详细描述了这些飞碟:一个已损坏,另一个几乎完好无损。它们由2部分组成,一个直径约6英尺的驾驶舱或座舱。座舱周围环绕着一个直径18英尺、厚2英尺的圆环。座舱由类似铝的金属建造,但对该金属的实际分析无法得出结果。Coulter拥有一块金属碎片并将其交给福特公司的人送往迪尔伯恩(Dearborn)工厂进行分析。这个人(Coulter)向包括Fick在内的一群人展示了一个从飞碟上取下的时钟或自动日历。这个时钟或自动日历由3块金属以及某种不寻常类型的金属组成。在其中1或2块金属的表面上有一个凹痕,该凹痕围绕圆盘旋转,每24天完成一个周期。

**Context:** 根据所提供的信息,在2年时间里,美国境内发现了大约50个这样的飞碟。其中40个位于洛杉矶的7个美国研究渠道中。每架飞行器有2名机组人员。损坏飞船中的尸体已烧焦,但另一艘飞船的乘员保存完好,尽管已经死亡。

**Note:** 该文件是对最初于1950年1月14日发送的贝克类别(情报)信息的转发。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Classified incoming message from COMSGENARMYTHREE Ft McPherson GA to Dept of Army for Director of Intelligence, dated 3 Mar 1950, reference TWX AJACI-1-2.

**Sighting:** At 2130 hours on 2nd March, radar station picked up 2 objects at 310 degrees azimuth, altitude 80,000 feet, approximately 18 miles from Knoxville in general direction of Oak Ridge. Objects were moving in circular motion but in opposite directions. At 2230 hours 2nd Mar and again at 0030 hours 3rd Mar, station picked up object moving same direction, locality and altitude.

**Object:** Density of object similar to DC-3 airplane. Speed not established but report describes it as "terrific".

**Follow-up Actions:** CIA Radar Technician reportedly arrives Knoxville to check radar set and operation. FBI made arrangement with Naval and Marine Reserve Unit Knoxville to set up radar equipment to verify reception of "UROL" radar station. All information on this subject turned over to A-2 Fourteenth Air Force.

**Note:** Message marked "PARAPHRASE NOT REQUIRED" and stamped for FBI with various routing annotations. Document shows coordination between Army, CIA, FBI, and Air Force intelligence units in investigating high-altitude radar contacts near sensitive Oak Ridge facility.

**Sighting:** 3月2日2130时，雷达站在方位角310度、高度80,000英尺处探测到2个物体，距离诺克斯维尔(Knoxville)约18英里，大致朝向橡树岭(Oak Ridge)方向。物体做圆周运动但方向相反。3月2日2230时及3月3日0030时，雷达站再次探测到物体沿相同方向、位置和高度移动。

**Object:** 物体密度类似DC-3飞机。速度未确定，但报告描述为"极快"。

**Follow-up Actions:** 据报CIA雷达技术员抵达诺克斯维尔检查雷达设备和操作。FBI与诺克斯维尔海军和海军陆战队预备役部队做出安排，架设雷达设备以验证"UROL"雷达站的接收情况。所有相关信息已移交第十四航空队A-2部门。

**Document:** This is page 2 of a classified incoming message (AJACI 1-2) from the Department of the Army Staff Communications Office, dated 3 March 1950. The message concerns administrative and operational issues related to radar operations at Oak Ridge.

**Key Points:**

**Personnel Issue:** Point 3 notes that "Third Army has no radar operators," indicating a staffing deficiency.

**Quality Control Request:** Point 4 reports that an inquiry from Lt Col Nunamaker revealed that the Chief Security Division at Oak Ridge "is anxious to get qualified personnel check on the performance of the radar." This suggests concerns about radar operational effectiveness or reliability at the sensitive Oak Ridge facility.

**Context:** Oak Ridge was a critical nuclear research and production facility during this period. The request for qualified personnel to check radar performance, combined with the lack of radar operators, indicates potential vulnerabilities in air defense or detection capabilities at this strategic location.

**Action:** The message designates action code G-2 (military intelligence), indicating the security implications of the radar personnel situation.

events.report_summary:
**Source:** Message from COMGENARMYTHREE Ft McPherson GA to Department of Army for Director of Intelligence, dated 2 March 1950. Document received via telephone call from Lt Col Tunamaker, Tennessee Military District 1130.

**Radar Station:** A radar station near Knoxville operated by station WROL had been in operation for approximately 3 weeks. The station was being run by WROL of Knoxville.

**First Detection (1 March):** On 1 March at 2135 hours (9:35 PM), the station picked up an object at 340 degrees and 18 miles from Knoxville at an altitude of 40,000 feet. Direction and distance placed the object directly over Oak Ridge. AEC Security Division Chief at Oak Ridge checked with Smyrna Air Base Nashville, which reported it had no flight plan for any plane being in that vicinity and altitude.

**Second Detection (2 March):** On 2 March at 1105 hours (11:05 AM), the station picked up an object at 335 degrees and 18 miles from Knoxville at altitude 40,000 feet. AEC Security Division Chief checked with Smyrna Air Base with negative results.

**Investigation:** AEC Sec Div Chief expressed uncertainty about operational efficiency of the radar unit and requested Smyrna AB send a qualified radar operator. Smyrna had no personnel available, so Smyrna Commander suggested Third Army send qualified radar operator to check equipment.

**Data Limitations:** Data from radar was limited to bearing, distance and altitude on each object. Third Army queried 14th Air Force to determine if 14th AF had training flights over the Knoxville area on 1 and 2 March. Answer was no.

**Note:** Document stamped "PARAPHRASE NOT REQUIRED" and marked CONFIDENTIAL. The proximity of detections to Oak Ridge facility appears significant given AEC Security Division involvement in verification efforts.

**Radar Station:** 诺克斯维尔(Knoxville)附近由WROL电台运营的雷达站已运行约3周。该站由诺克斯维尔的WROL负责运营。

**First Detection (1 March):** 3月1日2135时(晚上9:35)，该站在距诺克斯维尔340度方向18英里、高度40,000英尺处探测到一个物体。方向和距离显示该物体正处于橡树岭(Oak Ridge)正上方。橡树岭AEC安全部主管与纳什维尔斯米尔纳空军基地(Smyrna Air Base Nashville)核实，该基地报告没有任何飞机在该区域和高度的飞行计划。

**Second Detection (2 March):** 3月2日1105时(上午11:05)，该站在距诺克斯维尔335度方向18英里、高度40,000英尺处探测到一个物体。AEC安全部主管与斯米尔纳空军基地核实，结果为否定。

**Investigation:** AEC安全部主管对该雷达装置的运行效率表示不确定，要求斯米尔纳空军基地(Smyrna AB)派遣合格的雷达操作员。斯米尔纳无可用人员，因此斯米尔纳指挥官建议第三集团军(Third Army)派遣合格的雷达操作员检查设备。

**Data Limitations:** 雷达提供的数据仅限于每个物体的方位、距离和高度。第三集团军向第14航空队(14th Air Force)查询，以确定第14航空队在3月1日和2日是否在诺克斯维尔地区有训练飞行。答案是没有。

**Note:** 文件盖有"无需释义"(PARAPHRASE NOT REQUIRED)印章并标记为机密(CONFIDENTIAL)。鉴于AEC安全部参与核实工作，探测位置接近橡树岭设施似乎具有重要意义。

**Document:** Classified incoming message from COMGENARMYTHREE Ft McPherson Ga to Department of Army Director of Intelligence, dated 9 March 1950, marked PRIORITY and CONFIDENTIAL. Message number AJACI-3-5 3206, later declassified under authority NND 90986.

**Sighting:** Recurs earlier TWX AJACI-3-3 which reported radar sightings over Oakridge, Tennessee. Additional information indicates the radar operator was inexperienced and the radar set had been modified in a way that cast doubt on the reliability of readings.

**Recommendation:** Chief of Tennessee Military District recommends expeditious action be taken to determine whether an unknown object has reappeared over Oakridge in the past few days. Chief Security Division at Oakridge requested information as to channels of communication with Air Force in connection with radar sightings.

**Note:** Message references CM IN 12184 (4 Mar) Q-2. Document dated 20 MAR 1950, with ACTION: Q-2 and INFO: Q-3 designations. Also marked for FBI ("for: FBI" notation visible). Message forwarded to Director of Intelligence regarding unusual radar activity at sensitive nuclear facility.

**Significance:** Oakridge (Oak Ridge) was home to major nuclear research and production facilities, making radar anomalies particularly significant from a security perspective during early Cold War period.

events.report_summary:
**Document Overview:**
This is page 2 of a confidential summary document (File No: (24-8)-28) dated 25 May 1950, providing administrative background on the green fireball investigation in New Mexico. The document is signed by Lt Colonel Doyle Rees, USAF District Commander.

**Key Personnel:**
Dr. Lincoln LaPaz, Director of the Institute of Meteoritics and Head of the Department of Mathematics and Astronomy at the University of New Mexico, served as the primary scientific consultant. He was Research Mathematician at the New Mexico Proving Grounds under OSRD appointment in 1943-1944, and Technical Director of Operations Analysis Section, Headquarters Second Air Force, 1944-45. Since 1948, Dr. LaPaz served on a voluntary basis as consultant for this District in connection with the green fireball investigations.

**Conferences:**
On 17 February 1949 and again on 14 October 1949, conferences were held at Los Alamos, New Mexico, to discuss the green fireball phenomena. Representatives present included: Fourth Army, Armed Forces Special Weapons Project, University of New Mexico, Federal Bureau of Investigation, U.S. Atomic Energy Commission, University of California, U.S. Air Force Scientific Advisory Board, Geophysical Research Division Air Materiel Command USAF, and the Office of Special Investigations (IG) USAF.

**Conclusions:**
A logical explanation was not proffered with respect to the origin of the green fireballs. It was generally concluded that the phenomena existed and should be studied scientifically until the occurrences have been satisfactorily explained. The continued occurrence of unexplained phenomena near sensitive installations was cause for concern.

**Scientific Study:**
The Geophysical Research Division, Air Materiel Command, Cambridge, Massachusetts, recently let a contract to Land-Air, Inc., Holloman AFB, Alamogordo, New Mexico, for a limited scientific study of green fireballs. The results of this scientific approach were expected to be of great value in determining the origin of these phenomena.

**Purpose Statement:**
This summary was prepared to re-emphasize that phenomena have continuously occurred in the New Mexico skies during the past 18 months and are continuing to occur in the vicinity of sensitive military and government installations.

events.report_summary_zh:
**Document Overview:**
这是一份机密摘要文件的第2页(档案编号:(24-8)-28),日期为1950年5月25日,提供了新墨西哥州(New Mexico)绿色火球调查的行政背景信息。该文件由USAF地区指挥官Doyle Rees中校签署。

**Key Personnel:**
Lincoln LaPaz博士,新墨西哥大学陨石研究所所长兼数学与天文学系主任,担任主要科学顾问。他于1943-1944年在OSRD任命下担任新墨西哥试验场的研究数学家,1944-45年担任第二航空队司令部作战分析部门技术主任。自1948年以来,LaPaz博士以志愿者身份担任本地区绿色火球调查的顾问。

**Conferences:**
1949年2月17日和1949年10月14日,在新墨西哥州洛斯阿拉莫斯(Los Alamos)召开会议讨论绿色火球现象。与会代表包括:第四集团军、武装部队特种武器项目、新墨西哥大学、FBI、美国原子能委员会、加利福尼亚大学、USAF科学咨询委员会、USAF空军装备司令部地球物理研究部,以及USAF特别调查办公室(IG)。

**Conclusions:**
关于绿色火球的起源,未能提出合理的解释。普遍认为这种现象确实存在,应进行科学研究,直到这些现象得到令人满意的解释。在敏感设施附近持续发生的无法解释的现象引起了关注。

**Scientific Study:**
位于马萨诸塞州剑桥市(Cambridge, Massachusetts)的空军装备司令部地球物理研究部,最近与新墨西哥州阿拉莫戈多(Alamogordo)霍洛曼空军基地(Holloman AFB)的Land-Air公司签订合同,对绿色火球进行有限的科学研究。这种科学方法的结果预计对确定这些现象的起源具有重大价值。

**Purpose Statement:**
编写本摘要旨在重新强调,在过去18个月中,新墨西哥州上空持续发生这些现象,并且在敏感军事和政府设施附近继续发生。

**Witness:** Colonel Lertora of Stanfield, Holloman Air Force Base, New Mexico, observed and photographed an unknown aerial phenomena on 24 and 25 February 1950. Analysis was conducted by Dr. Lincoln LaPaz, Head of the Institute of Meteoritics at the University of New Mexico, Albuquerque.

**Object:** The photograph shows a perfectly round luminous object observed at Datil, New Mexico. Dr. LaPaz determined the angular diameter was approximately 1/4 of a degree. The object's angular velocity in the sky was greater than half a degree per minute.

**Analysis:** Dr. LaPaz concluded based on the angular diameter and velocity measurements that the object was:
- Not the moon (angular diameter too small)
- Not Venus or any other planet (angular diameter too large)
- Not a bright fixed star slightly out of focus (the observed rate of motion was double that due to the diurnal rotation of the earth)

**Note:** This sighting was officially designated as "Sighting No. 175" and was marked CONFIDENTIAL. The photograph appears to show a single bright circular object against a dark sky background.

- 不是月球(角直径太小)

- 不是轻微失焦的明亮恒星(观测到的运动速率是地球周日自转导致速率的两倍)

**Note:** 该目击事件被正式指定为"目击事件175号"(Sighting No. 175),并标记为机密(CONFIDENTIAL)。照片似乎显示在黑暗天空背景下有一个明亮的圆形物体。

events.title: Military jet pilots observe object at 8000 ft near Fairbanks, Alaska (15 Dec 1950)
events.source: FBI Case File 62-HQ-83894 Section 6 (17th OSI Dist), p.97
events.report_summary:
**Source:** Classified incoming message from COMSARAL FT RICHARDSON ALASKA to DEFTAR WASH DC FOR ACOPS G2, dated 15 December 1950. Transmitted via G-2 through MASON CHANNELS and declassified under authority NND 90986.

**Witness:** Military jet pilots flying over Meeks International Field at Fairbanks, Alaska.

**Sighting:** While flying at an altitude of 8000 feet, pilots observed a flash of light that appeared yellow in color. The light was positioned at an altitude between 25,000 and 30,000 feet. Horizontal distance to the object was approximately 40 to 50 miles. Shortly after the flash, a dark brown smoke appeared beginning to rise and climb at an angle of 40 degrees. At the leading edge of the smoke at approximately 100 feet appeared an object silhouetted against a snow-covered or fuselage-like shape without wings traveling at terrific speed.

**Object:** Pilots started pursuit on a heading of 210 degrees magnetic, indicating 380 at very steep climb. They continued pursuit until pilots reached the village of Clear and lost sight of the object. Meanwhile, the object gained altitude and speed and disappeared because of distance at approximately 50 to 55,000 feet. Color of smoke was medium brown. Color of object described as dark and no reflection from sunlight. Pilots assured of shape because of perfect silhouette against the sun. One pilot had object in view approximately 2 plus minutes.

**Tactics:** Pilots sighted the object at coordinates 64 degrees 13 mins North, 149 degrees 30 mins West. Additional information to be forwarded when obtained.

**Note:** Document marked CONFIDENTIAL PRIORITY. Multiple signatures visible including handwritten annotations. Action designated as G2. Info designated as G3, AF. CM IN 932.

events.report_summary_zh:
**Source:** 来自COMSARAL FT RICHARDSON ALASKA致DEFTAR WASH DC FOR ACOPS G2的机密来电，日期为1950年12月15日。通过G-2经MASON CHANNELS传输，根据NND 90986授权解密。

**Witness:** 飞越阿拉斯加费尔班克斯米克斯国际机场的军用喷气式飞机飞行员。

**Sighting:** 飞行员在8000英尺高度飞行时，观察到一道黄色闪光。该光源位于25,000至30,000英尺的高度。与该物体的水平距离约为40至50英里。闪光后不久，出现了深棕色烟雾，开始以40度角上升和爬升。在烟雾前缘约100英尺处，出现一个物体，其轮廓映衬在积雪上，呈现出类似机身的形状，没有机翼，以极快的速度飞行。

**Object:** 飞行员开始追击，航向为磁210度，以非常陡峭的爬升角度指示380。他们持续追击直到飞行员到达克利尔村(Clear)并失去该物体的视线。与此同时，该物体获得了高度和速度，并因距离原因在约50,000至55,000英尺处消失。烟雾颜色为中棕色。物体颜色被描述为深色，没有阳光反射。飞行员确信其形状，因为在阳光映衬下呈现出完美的轮廓。一名飞行员观察该物体约2分钟以上。

**Tactics:** 飞行员在北纬64度13分、西经149度30分的坐标处发现该物体。获得更多信息后将转发。

**Note:** 文件标记为机密优先(CONFIDENTIAL PRIORITY)。可见多个签名，包括手写批注。行动指定为G2。信息指定为G3、AF。CM IN 932。

events.source: FBI Case File 62-HQ-83894 Section 6 (17th OSI Dist), p.101
events.report_summary:
**Document:** Summary of information regarding unconventional aircraft sighted over Oak Ridge, Tennessee, submitted by 111th CIC to comply with Third Army Headquarters letter AJ40T-360.33 General dated 15 November 1950.

**Location & Time:** Sighting occurred between 0320 and 0530 hours on 18 December 1950, on the Turnpike within the controlled area, approximately one (1) mile from the White Wing entrance and Y-12 plant.

**Weather:** At 0730 hours - wind from the Northeast at seven (7) miles per hour; temperature -20 degrees F, according to the Atomic Energy Commission Meteorological Division.

**Witnesses:** Multiple credible witnesses including Dr. A. J. Miller (518 Delaware Avenue), Dr. E. P. Calkins (105 Dieston Road), Mr. J. Frank Coneybear (119 Meadow Road), Mr. A. C. Mooneyham (101 Dewey Road), Mr. T. M. Fily (331 East Villanova Road), Lt. Col. John R. Hood (U.S.A.F., 200 Virginia Road), Cdr. E. W. Briber (U.S.N., 103 Morris Lane), and Maj. Lester L. Oates (U.S.A.F., HEP Division, Fairchild Engine and Airplane Corporation).

**Object:** A light emanating in the shape of a circle, with intensity much greater than that of a bright moon, giving the impression of form in connection with the light. The light was white in appearance and did not show any signs of refraction into a band or continuous spectrum. The object traveled in a Northwesterly direction, 15 to 30 degrees elevation above the horizon, and appeared to diminish considerable in size during thirty seconds of observation. To another group, the object appeared only as a bright reflection of the sun from an apparent metal surface. No accurate estimate of the object's size or range could be made from the observation.

**Note:** Additional information quoted from the Radar Log maintained by the McGhee Tyson Air Force Radar Station referenced in document as Enclosure.

**Witnesses:** Personnel of the 663rd AC&W Squadron and the 5th Air Fighter Squadron, McGhee Tyson Airport, Knoxville, Tennessee.

**Object Sighted:** The radar log of the 663rd AW and C Squadron, McGhee Tyson Airport, Knoxville, Tennessee contained the following entry: "20 December 1950. 1247 hours. Small paint in area (Oak Ridge Controlled Area). Very, very slow. Made perfect intercept (with F-82 Fighter aircraft) and orbit surrounding small smoke cloud."

**Photographs:** None available.

**Note:** This report was made because of its possible aid in determining the identity of numerous unidentified objects sighted over Oak Ridge, Tennessee. Source information came from personnel of 663rd AC&W Squadron, McGhee Tyson, Knoxville, Tennessee, and the log of the 663rd AC&W Squadron.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Report dated 20 January 1951 from 111th CIC Detachment, submitted in compliance with letter AMGOT-360.33 General, dated 15 November 1950, regarding unconventional aircraft sightings.

**Location and Time:** Radar sighting occurred for approximately three hours beginning at 1605 hours on 14 December 1950, on the Radar Scopes of the 663rd AC and W Squadron, McGhee Tyson Airport, Knoxville, Tennessee.

**Weather:** At 1600 hours on 14 December 1950: Ceiling 2100 feet, broken overcast; visibility seven (7) miles; Temperature 37 degrees F.; wind Southwest at thirteen (13) miles per hour.

**Witnesses:** Personnel of the 663rd AC and W Squadron, 30th Air Division, McGhee Tyson Airport, Knoxville, Tennessee, who were on duty at the time. Their occupations listed as radar operators, supervisors, and experts.

**Object Sighted:** A group of targets blanketed the Radar Scopes in the area directly over the government Atomic Energy Commission projects at Oak Ridge, Tennessee. These objects could not be identified from the radar image and a perfect fighter interception met with negative results.

**Investigation:** Lt. Robinson of the 663rd AC and W Squadron took photographs of the scope readings with a personal, four (4) by five (5) Speed Graphic camera using Plus-X film (ASA 50) at lens opening of F-2 and a shutter speed varying from twenty (20) to forty-five (45) seconds. The negatives were printed and forwarded to the 30th Air Division, Selfridge Air Force Base, Michigan, for investigation printed on negatives and sent copies thereon to the 663rd AC and W Squadron. The numerous targets can readily be identified from the permanent radar echos by comparing the photographs.

**Source:** Personnel and logs of the 663rd AC and W Squadron, McGhee Tyson Airport, Knoxville, Tennessee.

events.title: Multiple unidentified aerial objects sighted over Oak Ridge, Tennessee (16 Jan 1951)
events.source: FBI Case File 62-HQ-83894 Section 6 (17th OSI Dist), p.109
events.report_summary:
**Document:** Report from 111th CIC Detachment, FAO #8, regarding unusual aerial incidents over Oak Ridge, Tennessee, dated 20 January 1950 (likely 1951 based on content dates). The Commanding Officer of the 663rd AC&W Squadron forwarded a letter dated 17 January 1951 detailing multiple sightings.

**Initial Sighting (1915 hours, 16 Jan 1951):** An unusual airborne object was sighted approximately 10 miles WNW of the station. The lighted object appeared similar to a star but much brighter and slightly larger than other stars. The object appeared to be approximately 6,000 feet above terrain and descending slowly. As it approached the Oak Ridge Area, AEC Patrol Headquarters was notified and their ground observers alerted. Interference was noted on Radar Scopes (AN/CPS-11) in the approximate area of the object; however, no interference was noted on the height finder (AN/CPS-4).

**Subsequent Attempts (1925 hours):** Object still in approximate location; AEC again notified to attempt interception, but still no report from AEC Headquarters.

**Second Sighting (1930 hours):** Similar object observed 15 to 20 miles east of station; appears to be ascending rather than descending.

**Aircraft Investigation (1935 hours):** AF 7177 (legally homed and piloted by named and assigned officer) contacted GCA to investigate. The aircraft was directed to steer to object approximately 25 miles SW of station. Pilot Major Raymond C. Cave requested to investigate object east of station.

**Resolution (1945 hours):** AF 7177 sighted subject object and reported it to be a star.

**Additional Observations (1945-1955 hours):** F-82 orbiting S/E corner of Oak Ridge Area reported no electronic or visual observation. Visual observation reported by Oak Ridge Ground Observers 12 miles southeast of X-25 area (SE corner of Oak Ridge Area) with F-82 in sight and north of object. F-82 vectored south toward object but made no contact, electronic or visual. Object reported 2400 feet above terrain by Oak Ridge observers. Oak Ridge Patrol Headquarters later reports that observed object determined to be a star.

**Note:** Multiple military and civilian observers involved; radar interference noted but inconclusive; objects ultimately identified as stars, though initial appearance and behavior suggested something more unusual.

events.report_summary_zh:
**Document:** 来自第111反间谍队(CIC)分遣队FAO #8的报告，关于田纳西州橡树岭(Oak Ridge)上空不寻常空中事件，报告日期为1950年1月20日(根据内容日期可能是1951年)。第663 AC&W中队指挥官转发了一封1951年1月17日的信件，详细描述了多次目击事件。

**Initial Sighting(初次目击，1951年1月16日1915时):** 在距离站点西北偏西约10英里处目击到一个不寻常的空中物体。该发光物体看起来类似星体，但比其他星星更亮且稍大。该物体似乎位于地形上方约6,000英尺处并缓慢下降。当它接近橡树岭地区时，AEC巡逻总部接到通知，地面观测员保持警戒。在雷达显示器(AN/CPS-11)上该物体大致区域出现干扰;然而，测高仪(AN/CPS-4)上未发现干扰。

**Subsequent Attempts(后续尝试，1925时):** 物体仍在大致位置;再次通知AEC尝试拦截，但仍未收到AEC总部的报告。

**Second Sighting(第二次目击，1930时):** 在站点以东15至20英里处观测到类似物体;似乎在上升而非下降。

**Aircraft Investigation(飞机调查，1935时):** AF 7177(合法归航并由指定军官驾驶)联系GCA进行调查。该飞机被引导转向站点西南约25英里处的物体。飞行员Raymond C. Cave少校请求调查站点以东的物体。

**Resolution(结论，1945时):** AF 7177目击到目标物体并报告其为一颗星体。

**Additional Observations(补充观测，1945-1955时):** F-82在橡树岭地区东南角盘旋，报告未发现电子或视觉观测结果。橡树岭地面观测员报告在X-25区域(橡树岭地区东南角)东南12英里处进行视觉观测，F-82在视野内且位于物体北侧。F-82被引导向南朝物体方向飞行，但未取得接触，无论电子还是视觉。橡树岭观测员报告物体位于地形上方2400英尺。橡树岭巡逻总部后来报告观测到的物体确定为星体。

**Note:** 涉及多名军方和民间观测员;注意到雷达干扰但无定论;物体最终被确认为星体，尽管最初的外观和行为暗示了某些更为不寻常的东西。

events.location: Ritchie Highway near US Route 301, Baltimore, Maryland
events.title: Disc-shaped object sighted near Baltimore, MD (29 Mar 1952)
events.source: FBI Case File 62-HQ-83894 Section 6 (17th OSI Dist), p.153
events.report_summary:
**Investigation:** USAF Office of Special Investigations conducted investigation at request of Hq. OSI based on information from Air Technical Intelligence Center at Wright-Patterson AFB. Two witnesses, DONALD STEWART (FAU) and TYLER, had reported observing unconventional type aircraft on 29 March 1952 near Baltimore, Maryland.

**Primary Witness (STEWART):** DONALD STEWART, 224 Warren Avenue and Govans, Maryland, 111-C East Montgomery Road, Baltimore, interviewed on 24 and 27 April 1952. Stewart reported sighting a disc-like object at approximately 2045 hours on 29 March 1952 on Ritchie Highway near intersection of US Route 301.

**Object Description:** Automobile engine stopped and paint cracked as aircraft hovered 200 feet above ground. STEWART interviewed and related substantially same story he had given to news commentator LOU CORBIN of station WFBR, Baltimore.

**Investigation Results:** HAY FOX, Engineer at Westinghouse Electric Corporation Baltimore, interviewed and advised he had made complete examination of STEWART's vehicle at CORBIN's request, including examination with geiger counter, and determined no unusual effects. ARGOS interviewed, stated had no direct knowledge of incident and had merely relayed information furnished by CORBIN. Several residents of Gibson Island, Maryland had heard unusual noises but none had observed any such aircraft.

**Follow-up:** WIARD interviewed and confirmed statement given to STEWART; however, upon reinterview, admitted he had not been with STEWART at time of alleged sighting and had not seen any such aircraft. STEWART had asked him to tell that story and that he had done so. Interviews conducted along Ritchie Highway in vicinity of location where aircraft allegedly sighted.

events.source: FBI Case File 62-HQ-83894 Section 6 (17th OSI Dist), p.156
events.report_summary:
**Witness:** Donald F. Stewart, clerk employed by Baltimore & Ohio Railroad, and George S. Tyler III observed a strange appearing aircraft on 29 March 1952. The observation occurred near Ritchie Highway at the harness track at 10:45 PM under clear weather with moon and stars visible.

**Sighting:** The observation lasted approximately two (2) minutes at an estimated altitude of two hundred (200) feet. Weather conditions were clear with NNE winds at twelve (12) miles per hour and winds aloft at one thousand (1000) feet at NNE sixteen (16) miles per hour.

**Investigation:** On 10 May 1952, Mr. Louis E. Corbin was interviewed at radio station WFBR in Baltimore, Maryland. Corbin had received information about the incident in late April from Donald F. Stewart. Corbin was a newspaper reporter for local newspapers interested in the "flying saucer situation" and intended to write a documentary program for broadcast. As the first incident brought to his attention in that area, he determined to investigate it. On 24 April 1952, Corbin interviewed Mr. Stewart and obtained detailed chronological information about the sighting.

**Note:** Corbin advised he was acquainted with the editor of a civilian intelligence bulletin, Mr. Elias Louis Amoss, to whom he communicated the information. Corbin stated he would not release any information publicly until authorities completed their investigation. When Corbin called Anne Arundel County Police, they informed him they had numerous reports of that nature but had passed them off as harmless. Corbin had a friend, Raymond Fox, conduct a scientific examination of Stewart's automobile to determine any unusual characteristics which might have been present. Corbin was not a reserve CIC officer but had been an intelligence officer with the staff of General George S. Patton in Europe and presently held an inactive reserve commission as lieutenant colonel, 0-375086.

**Sighting:** 观察持续了大约2分钟，估计高度为200英尺。天气状况晴朗，北北东风速12英里/小时，1000英尺高空风向为北北东，风速16英里/小时。

**Investigation:** 1952年5月10日，路易斯·E·科宾(Louis E. Corbin)先生在马里兰州巴尔的摩市的WFBR广播电台接受了访谈。科宾在4月下旬从唐纳德·F·斯图尔特处获得了关于该事件的信息。科宾是当地报纸的新闻记者，对"飞碟情况"很感兴趣，并打算撰写一个纪录片节目进行广播。作为该地区引起他注意的第一起事件，他决定对其进行调查。1952年4月24日，科宾采访了斯图尔特先生，并获得了关于该目击事件的详细时间顺序信息。

**Note:** 科宾表示他认识一份民间情报公报的编辑埃利亚斯·路易斯·阿莫斯(Elias Louis Amoss)先生，并向他传达了这一信息。科宾声称在当局完成调查之前，他不会公开发布任何信息。当科宾致电安妮阿伦德尔县(Anne Arundel County)警方时，警方告知他们收到过许多类似性质的报告，但都将其视为无害而不予重视。科宾让他的朋友雷蒙德·福克斯(Raymond Fox)对斯图尔特的汽车进行科学检查，以确定是否存在任何可能出现的异常特征。科宾并非CIC预备役军官，但曾在欧洲担任乔治·S·巴顿(George S. Patton)将军参谋部的情报官员，目前持有中校非现役预备役军官委任状，军官编号0-375086。

events.title: Flying saucer scare: retired officer suggests atomic bomb energy theory (1 Aug 1952)
events.record_description: The FBI's 62-HQ-83894 case file includes investigative records, eyewitness testimonies, and public reports concerning Unidentified Flying Objects and flying discs documented between June 1947 and July 1968. The records include high-profile incident accounts, photographic evidence from sites like Oak Ridge, TN, and technical proposals regarding potential propulsion systems. Additional topics include convention programs, researcher accounts, and extensive media coverage from the period. events.report_summary:
**Witness:** Edmond J. Kane, a retired member of the St. Paul Police Force, veteran of both World War I and World War II, and 32-year member of the American Legion. Kane was a member of American Legion Post #81 of Mauston, Wisconsin (known as the Burton-Koppang Post). He had previous contacts with FBI agents Clintonstein and Samy Hardy.

**Theory:** Kane wrote to FBI Director J. Edgar Hoover proposing that "flying saucers scare seems possible that the released energy of exploded Atomic Bombs could be soaring around in the atmosphere." He suggested this theory might help track down the source of the flying saucer phenomenon and relieve tension in the American public.

**Purpose:** The letter was not reporting a specific sighting, but rather offering a theoretical explanation for the widespread flying saucer reports occurring during the summer 1952 UFO wave. Kane requested FBI comments on his hypothesis and asked for acknowledgment and advice.

**Document Details:** The letter was recorded by the FBI on August 4, 1952 (RECORDED-119). It was filed in the FBI's personal files and marked as "Expedite." Reference number 65-83874-303 appears on the document. Handwritten notations include "O Flying Saucers" and various filing stamps.

**Witness:** 埃德蒙·J·凯恩(Edmond J. Kane)，圣保罗警察局退休成员，第一次世界大战和第二次世界大战的老兵，美国退伍军人协会(American Legion)32年会员。凯恩是威斯康星州莫斯顿(Mauston, Wisconsin)美国退伍军人协会第81分会(伯顿-科庞分会/Burton-Koppang Post)的成员。他此前曾与FBI特工克林顿斯坦(Clintonstein)和萨米·哈迪(Samy Hardy)有过接触。

**Theory:** 凯恩致信FBI局长J·埃德加·胡佛(J. Edgar Hoover)，提出"飞碟恐慌似乎有可能是原子弹爆炸释放的能量在大气层中盘旋"的理论。他认为这一理论可能有助于追踪飞碟现象的来源，并缓解美国公众的紧张情绪。

**Purpose:** 该信函并非报告具体的目击事件，而是为1952年夏季UFO浪潮期间广泛出现的飞碟报告提供一种理论解释。凯恩请求FBI对他的假设发表意见，并要求得到确认和建议。

The records include high-profile incident accounts, photographic evidence from sites like Oak Ridge, TN, and technical proposals regarding potential propulsion systems. events.report_summary:
**Document:** Letter from Robert D. Wolf, Director of Johnson County Department of Civil Defense (Franklin, Indiana), to J. Edgar Hoover, Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation, dated 20 January 1953.

**Purpose:** Wolf apologizes for writing directly to Hoover rather than through the State Director, but explains he has cleared this procedure with state authorities. He inquires whether the FBI has vetted or cleared an organization called the "International Flying Saucer Bureau."

**Context:** Wolf reports success with their Ground Observation Corps, operating four (4) posts in Johnson County. The previous fall, a local businessman contacted him about joining the International Flying Saucer Bureau. Wolf expressed interest in having local citizens interested in flying saucers also work in the Civil Defense program. Franklin is located approximately 20 miles southwest of Indianapolis on dual-lane highway U.S. #31.

**Request:** Wolf encloses a letter received in October and the current issue of "SPACE REVIEW." He asks the FBI to expedite information back to his office regarding whether this organization "has been cleared or is subversive in any way" so that he can determine next steps for enlisting interested persons in their program. Wolf requests return of enclosures if not required.

**Note:** The letter demonstrates Cold War-era vigilance regarding potential subversive organizations and the intersection between civilian UFO interest groups and official Civil Defense programs. Wolf's home address is listed as 19 North Forsythe St., Franklin, Indiana. Document stamped "RECORDED-84" and "INDEXED-84" with date 13 Feb 1953.

**Purpose:** 沃尔夫为直接致信胡佛而非通过州主任致歉,但解释说他已就此程序与州当局取得许可。他询问FBI是否已审查或核准一个名为"国际飞碟局"(International Flying Saucer Bureau)的组织。

**Context:** 沃尔夫报告其地面观测队(Ground Observation Corps)运作顺利,在约翰逊县设有四(4)个观测哨所。去年秋天,一位当地商人就加入国际飞碟局一事与他联系。沃尔夫表示有意让对飞碟感兴趣的当地公民也参与民防计划。富兰克林(Franklin)位于印第安纳波利斯(Indianapolis)西南约20英里处,在双车道高速公路U.S. #31上。

**Note:** 该信函体现了冷战时期对潜在颠覆性组织的警惕态度,以及民间UFO兴趣团体与官方民防计划之间的交集。沃尔夫的家庭住址列为印第安纳州富兰克林市北福赛思街(North Forsythe St.)19号。文件盖有"RECORDED-84"(已记录-84)和"INDEXED-84"(已编索引-84)印章,日期为1953年2月13日。

events.location: Allied Operations over Germany (SHAEF Air Staff, A-2)
events.title: SHAEF Air Staff memo: "Foo Fighters" night phenomena — Me-262s or rockets? (18 Mar 1945)
events.record_description: This file contains SHAEF messages and memorandums related to "night phenomena (foofighters)," flak rockets, unidentified cylindrical objects, and blinking lights. The documents include multiple references to the observations of the 415th Night Fighter Squadron.
events.report_summary:
**Memo from SHAEF Air Staff** (Supreme Headquarters Allied Expeditionary Force), file SHAEF/A/TS.37253/A.P., dated **18 March 1945**. Signed C. H. Geffers, Air Commodore, A.C. of S., A-2, for the Deputy Supreme Commander. Filed 4356 / TS Control 2354.

**Subject:** Night Phenomena.

**To:** First Tactical Air Force (Prov.), AAF AF, US ARMY.

**Body:**
1. With reference to reports forwarded from the **IIIrd Tactical Air Command** through your Headquarters on the subject of **night phenomena ('foo fighters')**, and further to this Headquarters' letter of even reference dated 11 February, **no reply has been received from the Air Ministry**, who say that **Bomber Command crews have for some time been reporting similar phenomena.**

2. The **Air Ministry view is that a few of the alleged aircraft may have been Me-262s, and for the rest, that rockets are suggested as the most likely explanation.**

3. It is regretted that no further or more definite information can be given.

**Historical context:** This is the famous **'foo fighters'** wartime UAP phenomenon — luminous balls of light reported by Allied bomber and night-fighter crews flying over Germany and occupied Europe in 1944–1945. SHAEF Air Staff sought an explanation but the Air Ministry, after months of inquiry, could only suggest the new German Me-262 jet (just entering combat) or rockets — even though many sightings were of objects behaving in ways that did not match either. The 'foo fighter' reports are now considered the earliest large-scale modern UAP wave.
events.report_summary_zh:
**SHAEF空军参谋部备忘录**（盟军远征军最高司令部），档案编号SHAEF/A/TS.37253/A.P.，日期**1945年3月18日**。签署人：C. H. Geffers，空军准将，A.C. of S.，A-2，代表最高司令部副司令。归档编号4356 / TS Control 2354。

**主题：** 夜间现象。

**收件人：** 第一战术空军（临时），AAF AF，美国陆军。

**正文：**
1. 关于**第三战术航空司令部**通过贵司令部转呈的有关**夜间现象（'foo fighters'）**的报告，以及本司令部2月11日同参考编号的信函，**尚未收到英国空军部的答复**，空军部称**轰炸机司令部机组人员报告类似现象已有一段时间。**

2. **英国空军部的观点是，所称飞行器中可能有少数是Me-262战斗机，其余的，火箭被认为是最可能的解释。**

3. 遗憾的是无法提供更多或更明确的信息。

**历史背景：** 这是著名的战时**'foo fighters'（幽灵战斗机）**UAP现象——1944-1945年间，盟军轰炸机和夜间战斗机机组在德国及被占领的欧洲上空飞行时报告的发光球体。SHAEF空军参谋部寻求解释，但英国空军部经过数月调查，只能推测是刚投入战斗的德国新型Me-262喷气式战斗机或火箭——尽管许多目击描述的物体行为方式与两者都不符。'foo fighters'报告现被认为是最早的大规模现代UAP浪潮。

events.report_summary:
**Cover transmission** within Top Secret folder '341_110448 Records Relating to the Collection and Dissemination of Intelligence 1948-1955, TS Container No. 2, 2-5300 to 2-5399.'

**TWX TT 1524** from USAFE (United States Air Forces in Europe) to **General Cabell** (then USAF Director of Intelligence), dated **4 November 1948**.

**Body:** 'We now have one complete set of all reports prepared by special intelligence organization of the European Command from its inception to present date. We are forwarding these reports for your inspection and final disposition. We are of the opinion that inspection of these reports will lend weight to arguments for allocating Air Force funds to this organization. Advise caution in utilizing these reports as most of them were forwarded as received.'

**Note:** This is a compendium of European Command intelligence reports (likely including UAP/'flying-disc' material from Scandinavia, the Netherlands and Germany during the 1946–1948 'ghost-rocket' and post-war flying-saucer waves) being forwarded for review by HQ USAF Director of Intelligence. The original event extraction tagged the date as 8 November 1948 with location 'Netherlands' — the underlying records likely contain Dutch sightings from that period (e.g. the 1946 Swedish 'ghost rocket' overflights that extended into the Netherlands), but no specific 8 Nov 1948 Dutch sighting is visible in this folder's cover memo.

events.title: Misrep undefined-8584059: F-16CM INHERENT RESOLVE Mission, Multiple UAP Observed
events.record_description:
This document is a Mission Report (MISREP), a standardized reporting form the U.S. Military uses to record the circumstances surrounding its operations. U.S. military services often use MISREPs to report Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) to AARO. The GENTEXT, or “general text” section of these reports often contains important qualitative, contextual information, distinguishing it from the more quantitative, or numerical, data found elsewhere in the report.
A U.S. military operator reported observing “several bright objects maneuvering quickly” west to east northeast. The operator reported achieving a track on the UAP via an onboard targeting pod for approximately 20 seconds. The report describes that UAP then dimmed and disappeared from the targeting pod.
All descriptive and estimative language contained in this report reflects the reporter’s subjective interpretation at the time of the event. Such characterizations should not be interpreted as a conclusive indication of the presence or absence of any intrinsic object features or performance characteristics.
events.report_summary:
**Mission Overview**

A 2-ship formation of F-16CM aircraft took off from Prince Sultan Air Base (OEPS) on March 23, 2011, as part of Operation INHERENT RESOLVE. The flight was tasked to conduct Defensive Counter-Air (DCA) operations in the ESSA (presumably Iraq/Syria theater).

**Timeline of Events**

At 2007Z (14a timeblock), the flight entered IZ airspace (Iraq) with no issues reported (NFTR - Nothing Further To Report). At 2058Z, the flight entered SY airspace (Syria) and checked on-station with KINGPIN to conduct DCA in the ESSA area.

At 2302Z, the flight **observed multiple POSS CAPS (possible capsules/objects)** - reference is made to a separate UAP report for details.

At 0000Z, the flight checked off-station with KINGPIN and proceeded to return to base (RTB) at OEPS with no significant issues (NSTR). The flight exited IZ airspace at 0046Z and landed at OEPS with Explosive Ordnance Disposal (ESD) present at 0215Z.

**Classification Notes**

This report was originally classified SECRET//NOFORN and declassified on October 8, 2025, by MG Richard A. Harrison, USCENTCOM Chief of Staff. The operation was INHERENT RESOLVE, the U.S. military campaign against ISIS. Associated caveats are marked as NOFORN (Not Releasable to Foreign Nationals). Mission Source classification guide ID: MS, reference number 20480401.

Russians denied any of the claims and said that it could have been UFOs.  Cable authors note that Russians typically engage in the “bold lie” when they wish to conceal actions.

**Document Type:** U.S. State Department cable from Embassy Moscow (MRN 01 MOSCOW 13169), declassified in full on 2/25/2026.

**Parties Involved:** U.S. Embassy Moscow, SECSTATE Washington DC, USMISSION OSCE, AMEMBASSY Tbilisi (Tbilisi, Georgia), AMEMBASSY Baku (Azerbaijan), AMEMBASSY Yerevan (Armenia), USMISSION New York, and the Moscow Political Collective. Distribution included Joint Staff Washington DC and SECDEF.

**Subject:** "UFOs Over Georgia: Strange Encounters of an MFA Kind" — Reference to alleged Russian aircraft violations of Georgian airspace and bombing incidents in the Kodori Gorge region on October 28-29, 2001.

**Key Details:** This cable was transmitted with ROUTINE priority on October 30, 2001 (cable date 3000002 Oct 01). The Georgian Foreign Ministry alleged that Russian aircraft had violated Georgian airspace and bombed areas of the Kodori Gorge. Russian authorities denied all claims, suggesting instead that the incidents could have been UFOs. Cable authors noted that Russians typically engage in what they characterize as the "bold lie" tactic when attempting to conceal military actions.

**Classification:** Originally marked CONFIDENTIAL, declassified in full by John Powers, Acting-Director, U.S. Department of State. Tags include PREL (Preliminary), MARR (Military Affairs), KCFE, UN, OSCE, GG (Georgia), and RS (Russia).

events.title: Orbs Launching Orbs - Multiple Federal Agent Sightings
events.record_description: This document is a summary of statements by seven US PERSONs employed by the federal government who separately reported observing several unidentified anomalous phenomena in the western United States over the course of two days in 2023.  The summary notes the US PERSONS reported four distinct categories of experiences, including observing “orbs launching other orbs” at a distance, observing a large stationary glowing orb at close estimated range, pursuing a large phenomenon near the ground, and observing a large, seemingly transparent phenomenon, reported to being akin to a “translucent kite.” Although there is no technical data directly associated with this report, contextual factors — such as these events sharing features with others reported to the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), the reporters’ credibility, and the potentially anomalous nature of the events themselves — combine to make this report among the most compelling within AARO’s current holdings.
events.report_summary:
**Document Type:** AARO summary report of witness statements from federal law enforcement special agents.

**Witnesses:** Six federal law enforcement special agents (USPER1-USPER6) from three two-person teams independently observed and reported anomalous aerial phenomena.

**Event Description:** Over a two-day period at dusk in the western United States, multiple federal agents independently observed orange "orbs" in the sky that appeared to emit or launch smaller red "orbs" in groups of two to four. The consensus among witnesses was three red orbs per event. This phenomenon occurred at least five times across the two-day period.

**Behavior Patterns:** The orange orb would appear briefly (one to two seconds), launch the red orbs, then disappear. Red orbs generally moved away from the orange "mother" orb in horizontal paths. In some instances, one red orb moved "heading up at an angle," and witnesses reported red orbs would sometimes "swoop down" after launch. Events were observed from multiple locations and vantage points.

**Uncertainty:** Due to the sequential nature of observations, it remains unclear whether a single orange "mother" orb was involved or multiple orange orbs were present during the two-day period.

**Significance:** AARO considers this among the most compelling reports in their holdings due to witness credibility, shared features with other reports, and the potentially anomalous nature of the phenomena.

**Event Description:** 在美国西部黄昏时分的两天时间里，多名联邦特工独立观察到天空中出现橙色"球体"，这些球体似乎发射或释放出较小的红色"球体"，每次2至4个成组出现。证人的共识是每次事件有三个红色球体。这一现象在两天内至少发生了五次。

**Behavior Patterns:** 橙色球体会短暂出现(一至两秒)，发射红色球体，然后消失。红色球体通常沿水平路径远离橙色"母"球体。在某些情况下，一个红色球体"以一定角度向上移动"，证人报告称红色球体有时会在发射后"向下俯冲"。这些事件从多个地点和观察点被观测到。

**Uncertainty:** 由于观察的连续性质，目前尚不清楚两天期间是涉及单个橙色"母"球体，还是存在多个橙色球体。

**Significance:** AARO认为这是其掌握的最令人信服的报告之一，原因在于证人的可信度、与其他报告的共同特征，以及该现象潜在的异常性质。

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Headquarters Air Defense Command, Mitchel Field, New York, 18 September 1947. Summary of information received 12 August 1947 from Mr. Alpheus O. Powell, 26 Redwood Road, New Hyde Park, Long Island, regarding a flying disc sighting on 4 August 1947.

**Witness:** Alpheus O. Powell, Airlines Captain with Pan American Airways, Inc., first pilot of a Constellation aircraft on Flight from Gander, Newfoundland to La Guardia Field, New York.

**Flight Details:** Took over aircraft as Captain at Newfoundland and departed approximately 1230 P.M. Eastern Daylight Saving Time for La Guardia Field, New York. At 1600 P.M., position approximately abeam the Presque Isle-Fort Kent, Maine sector and the Bedford Station Beacon (Everett is 5 miles NW of Boston, Mass., and Bedford is 15 miles NW of the same city).

**Sighting:** Mr. W. White, navigator sitting in co-pilot's seat (right side of cockpit), first called Mr. Powell's attention to a bright orange object on the right side of the plane, slightly below the level of the aircraft. Mr. Powell unable to see the object initially due to visibility limitations from his position. Powell immediately glanced out his side window and noticed, at a 45° angle to the left, an unidentified flying object. It was about one mile away at an altitude of approximately 7,000 feet.

**Object Description:** Powell banked to obtain better view. Object was under observation for approximately 30 seconds. Powell described the object as being about the length of a P-40 fuselage, blunt at both ends, cylindrical in shape, and having a bright orange hue. Mr. Powell stated that the object had a definite shape and that there was no suggestion of gaseous dissipation as there would be if the orange color were the exhaust from a rocket or a jet aircraft. Powell estimated the course of the object to be 500° magnetic and that the object was traveling at approximately 160 mph.

**Outcome:** Mr. Powell lost sight of the object when a cloud came between the aircraft and the object. The pursuit of the object was not continued, inasmuch as it would have necessitated a departure from the established airways.

**Weather Conditions:** Visibility good; cloud coverage from 5-8/10ths, with tops at 10,000 feet and the base at the 3,000 foot level. Wind estimated at 270/25 miles per hour. Aircraft was at 9,000 feet; airspeed 265 mph; course 244 degrees magnetic.

**Witness:** 阿尔菲厄斯·O·鲍威尔（Alpheus O. Powell），泛美航空公司（Pan American Airways, Inc.）航线机长，星座式飞机从纽芬兰甘德（Gander, Newfoundland）飞往纽约拉瓜迪亚机场（La Guardia Field, New York）航班的第一飞行员。

**Sighting:** 领航员W·怀特先生（W. White）坐在副驾驶座位（驾驶舱右侧），首先提醒鲍威尔先生注意飞机右侧一个明亮的橙色物体，位置略低于飞机高度。鲍威尔先生最初因其位置的能见度限制无法看到该物体。鲍威尔立即从侧窗向外望去，注意到在左侧45°角方向有一个不明飞行物。该物体距离约1英里，高度约7,000英尺。

**Object Description:** 鲍威尔转向以获得更好的视野。该物体被观察了约30秒。鲍威尔描述该物体大约有P-40战斗机机身的长度，两端钝圆，呈圆柱形，具有明亮的橙色色调。鲍威尔先生表示该物体具有明确的形状，没有气体消散的迹象，不像火箭或喷气式飞机排气产生的橙色那样。鲍威尔估计该物体的航向为磁方位500°，速度约为每小时160英里。

**Outcome:** 当一片云遮挡在飞机和物体之间时，鲍威尔先生失去了对该物体的视线。未继续追踪该物体，因为这将需要偏离既定航路。

**Weather Conditions:** 能见度良好；云量覆盖5-8/10，云顶高度10,000英尺，云底高度3,000英尺。风速估计为270度方向/每小时25英里。飞机高度9,000英尺；空速265英里/小时；航向磁方位244度。

events.report_summary:
Two FBI/Air Defense Command interview reports (Mitchel Field, NY) summarizing a twin-witness UAP sighting on 4 August 1947, ~1600 EDT, by the crew of a Pan American Airways Constellation aircraft enroute from Gander, Newfoundland to La Guardia Field, New York. The aircraft was at 8,000 ft, airspeed 285 mph, course 246° magnetic, at a position approximately midway between the Everett (Mass) Fan Marker and the Bedford Radio Beacon — about 10 miles NW of Boston.

Captain Alpheus C. Powell (Pan Am, 28 Redwood Road, New Hyde Park, Long Island) described the object as 'about the length of a P-40 fuselage, blunt at both ends, cylindrical in shape, and a bright orange hue,' roughly 1 mile away at ~7,900 ft altitude. He observed it through a 45° left side-window angle for about 30 seconds before a cloud occluded it; estimated heading 200° magnetic, ~100 mph. There was no suggestion of gaseous dissipation that would indicate a rocket or jet exhaust.

Navigator Walter I. White (Pan Am, 19-67 79th Street, Jackson Heights, NY), in the co-pilot seat, independently sighted a similar object on the right side at ~3 miles range, ~1,000 ft below their flight level — 'deep gold in color' with a reflective surface, ~16 ft long × 3-4 ft deep, elliptical and blunted at the ends, traveling easterly on a 110° magnetic course at ~175 mph. Total observation by White ~30 seconds before he alerted Powell; the pilot then banked left and the entire incident transpired in under a minute and a half.

**Weather at sighting:** ~6/10ths scattered cumulus, tops at 10,000 ft, 10 mile visibility, winds 270°/25 kt at 8,000 ft. White had served as a PAA navigator for five years (war service with PAA). Both witnesses provided independent descriptions that differ in color and apparent size; Powell and White were unable to confirm they were observing the same object, though the timing matches.

两份FBI/防空司令部访谈报告(纽约米切尔机场)总结了1947年8月4日东部夏令时约1600时的双证人UAP目击事件,目击者为泛美航空公司一架星座式客机的机组人员,该机正从纽芬兰甘德飞往纽约拉瓜迪亚机场。飞机当时位于8,000英尺高度,空速285英里/小时,航向磁246°,位置大约在埃弗里特(马萨诸塞州)扇形标和贝德福德无线电信标之间的中点——波士顿西北约10英里处。

机长阿尔菲厄斯·C·鲍威尔(Alpheus C. Powell,泛美航空,长岛新海德公园红木路28号)描述该物体"大约有P-40战斗机机身那么长,两端钝圆,圆柱形,呈明亮的橙色",距离约1英里,高度约7,900英尺。他通过左侧45°角的舷窗观察了约30秒,直到云层遮挡;估计航向磁200°,速度约100英里/小时。没有任何气体消散的迹象表明这是火箭或喷气式排气。

领航员沃尔特·I·怀特(Walter I. White,泛美航空,纽约杰克逊高地79街19-67号)当时坐在副驾驶位上,独立在右侧发现了一个类似物体,距离约3英里,比他们的飞行高度低约1,000英尺——"深金色",表面反光,长约16英尺×深3-4英尺,椭圆形且两端钝圆,以磁110°航向向东飞行,速度约175英里/小时。怀特观察了约30秒后向鲍威尔发出警报;随后飞行员向左转弯,整个事件在不到一分半钟内结束。

**目击时天气:** 约6/10疏散积云,云顶10,000英尺,能见度10英里,8,000英尺高度风向270°/风速25节。怀特曾担任泛美航空领航员五年(战时在泛美航空服役)。两位证人提供的独立描述在颜色和明显尺寸上有所不同;鲍威尔和怀特无法确认他们观察的是同一物体,尽管时间上吻合。

The records include high-profile incident accounts, photographic evidence from sites like Oak Ridge, TN, and technical proposals regarding potential propulsion systems. events.report_summary:
**Witness:** Staff Sergeant Ira L. Livingston, RA 14 153 972, Air Corps, with approximately 250 hours flying time as pilot and Armorer Gunner. Statement subscribed and sworn on 7 July 1947 before 1st Lt. James L. MacFarlane, Asst Adj.

**Sighting:** At 2045 hours on 6 July 1947, while eating supper at his residence at 1554 Meadow Lane, Green Acres, Birmingham, Alabama, witness was called outside by his next-door neighbor, Mr. Herman W. Sockwell, who reported "Flying Discs" outside. Witness immediately went to front yard to observe the objects.

**Object:** The objects appeared to the west of Birmingham, traveling in a south-eastern direction. They appeared approximately 2000 feet above the horizon at a 45-degree angle from observer's position at an unestimated distance. Objects were approximately two (2) feet in diameter, round in shape, producing a dim glow of light and traveling at an estimated speed of five (5) to six (6) hundred miles per hour.

**Behavior:** Objects appeared to be traveling in a definite arc rather than straight but not always in the same path. As soon as one was out of sight another would appear behind it, but not always in the same path. Witness saw one that seemed to come straight up. View of where it came from was obstructed by a nearby house; when it reached altitude of approximately 2000 feet, it started off in same direction as the others. Witness did not see more than one at a time and believes there were seven (7) to ten (10) total, though could have been only one making multiple passes.

**Appearance:** The discs were silent and appeared to be composed of a single light.

**Document:** Restricted statement, part of official Air Corps investigation into flying disc reports.

**Sighting:** 1947年7月6日20时45分，目击者在其位于阿拉巴马州伯明翰市绿地庄园(Green Acres)草地巷(Meadow Lane)1554号的住所用晚餐时，被隔壁邻居 Herman W. Sockwell 先生叫到外面，称看到"飞碟"。目击者立即前往前院观察这些物体。

**Object:** 这些物体出现在伯明翰(Birmingham)西侧，向东南方向飞行。从观察者位置看，它们在地平线上方约2000英尺处，仰角约45度，距离无法估计。物体直径约2英尺，呈圆形，发出微弱光芒，估计飞行速度为每小时500至600英里。

**Behavior:** 物体似乎沿着明确的弧线而非直线飞行，但并非总是沿相同路径。一个物体消失后，另一个会出现在其后方，但路径不总相同。目击者看到其中一个似乎垂直上升。其起飞位置被附近房屋遮挡；当它到达约2000英尺高度时，开始朝与其他物体相同的方向飞去。目击者未曾同时看到多个物体，认为总数约有7至10个，但也可能只是同一个物体多次飞过。

**Appearance:** 这些圆盘状物体无声，似乎由单一光源构成。

**Document:** 机密声明，属于空军对飞碟报告官方调查的一部分。

events.report_summary:
**Organization:** 1388th AAF Base Unit, APO 864, c/o Postmaster, New York, N.Y.

**Sighting Date & Time:** 00302 hours (3:02 AM), 11 July 1947, at Codroy, Newfoundland (59°03' W Long., 47°50' N Lat.)

**Object Characteristics:** Disc-shaped flying object, approximately the size of a barrel-head, dinner-plate, and a plane flying high. Flame-colored with a trail of lighter flame color. The trail gave the whole object a cone-like appearance. The disc was described as very bright with an after-glow. Speed was very high velocity, heading from northwest eastward at approximately 6,000 feet altitude.

**Witnesses:** Mr. John Legge, Mr. Wm. Evans, and Albert Samms of Codroy, Newfoundland. Mr. Legge and Mr. Evans were standing outside Mr. Legge's store when they both sighted the object. Albert Samms also observed it independently and reported what he had seen to his mother. Mrs. Samms stated that Albert was in no way alarmed and was alone on his way home when he sighted it.

**Witness Credibility:** Mr. Legge is considered reliable, approximately 40 years old, with considerable experience as foreman of airplane fire crews in Newfoundland where he was in charge of 300 men during the war. **Weather:** Clear, at dusk.

events.report_summary:
Interrogation taken at 1430 EFT on 16 July 1947 by Capt William H. Smith, Jr., Intelligence Officer of the 1388th AAF Base Unit, Newfoundland Base Command (APO 864), of John N. Merrman, Jr., Supervisor and Mechanic for Trans World Airways at Harmon Field, Newfoundland. Merrman had been associated with aviation since approximately 1938 and served as an Army aerial gunner during WWII (qualified to judge object size and range).

On the evening of 10 July 1947, while driving up over the mountain between Harmon Field and Stephenville Crossing, Newfoundland, Merrman's companion (Mr Woodruff) called his attention to the sky. Through the windshield Merrman observed a bluish-black vapor trail left behind by an unseen object. The object itself was not visible; only the trail was left behind.

The object had passed through scattered cloud cover (5,000 to 10,000 ft) and cut a clean gap in the clouds — 'like a knife had cut it' — with feathered edges 'similar to a weld, as if you cut a weld in half.' The trajectory was horizontal, holding the same course approximately North-Northeast. Merrman could not estimate the object's size since he never saw the object, only its track through the clouds.

events.report_summary:
**Document:** Statement of Mr. John P. Legge of Cordroy, Newfoundland, taken by Mercedes Burke of the Intelligence Office, Harmon Field, Newfoundland, on 17 July 1947. Marked RESTRICTED.

**Witness:** John P. Legge, resident of Cordroy, Newfoundland.

**Sighting:** At approximately 10:00 PM on 10 July 1947, while standing by his door, Legge observed what appeared to be a "FLYING SAUCER." The witness explicitly states it was definitely not a shooting star (though he had seen several before) nor an airplane. The object was traveling too fast and at too great a speed for an aircraft.

**Object Description:** The object appeared as a disc with a barrel-shaped head and a trail behind it. The circular portion looked to be about the size of a barrel head, approximately 15 feet long. The trail behind the disc made the whole object look cone-shaped. The circle was bright red in color, resembling a flame, while the after-glow (cone-shaped trail) was a fainter shade. The witness describes it as traveling at the rate of a shooting star but much closer, estimating roughly 6,000 feet altitude. The object was visible for about 15 seconds, came from the Northwest heading Eastward.

**Key Details:** Clear night with no clouds, just getting dark. Unlike a shooting star which leaves a temporary streak, this object left no streak—only the trail that appeared to travel behind the circle which looked like an after-glow. If it had been on fire, the witness states, the airplane would have fallen into the water.

**Comparison:** Legge notes that what he saw Thursday night resembled a shooting star in no way whatsoever—there was only one such object observed.

**Witnesses:** Document signed by John P. Legge and two additional witnesses (signatures partially legible).

**Document:** 约翰·P·莱格先生的陈述，莱格先生居住于纽芬兰科德罗伊(Cordroy, Newfoundland)，该陈述由纽芬兰哈蒙机场(Harmon Field)情报办公室的梅赛德斯·伯克(Mercedes Burke)于1947年7月17日记录。标记为限制级(RESTRICTED)。

**Witness:** 约翰·P·莱格(John P. Legge)，纽芬兰科德罗伊居民。

**Sighting:** 1947年7月10日大约晚上10:00，莱格站在自家门口时，观察到了一个看起来像是"飞碟"的物体。目击者明确表示，它绝对不是流星(尽管他之前见过几次流星)，也不是飞机。该物体飞行速度太快，对于飞行器来说速度过高。

**Object Description:** 该物体呈圆盘状，带有桶形头部和尾随的轨迹。圆形部分看起来大约有桶口大小，约15英尺长。圆盘后方的尾迹使整个物体看起来呈锥形。圆形部分呈亮红色,像火焰一样，而余晖(锥形尾迹)颜色较淡。目击者描述它以流星的速度飞行，但距离更近，估计高度约6,000英尺。该物体可见约15秒，从西北方向朝东飞行。

**Key Details:** 当晚晴朗无云，天刚黑下来。与流星会留下暂时性条纹不同，该物体没有留下条纹——只有跟随圆形物体后方的尾迹，看起来像余晖。目击者表示，如果是着火的话，飞机早就坠入水中了。

**Comparison:** 莱格指出，他周四晚上看到的东西与流星完全不同——只观察到一个这样的物体。

**Witnesses:** 文件由约翰·P·莱格和另外两名目击者签名(签名部分可辨)。
